text:
New Jersey arrives with its record better than its luck. The Devils are 4-1-0 in their last five and beat Washington 5-2 two days ago, a game they took 60% of the expected goals in (expected goals measure the quality of chances). They're a +15 in goal difference on +21.0 expected, with goaltending costing them 5.4 goals above expected. They play without Johnathan Kovacevic and Anthony Mantha, and Connor Brown has taken Mantha's spot beside Rodrigues and Boqvist, up to 17:13 a night from 14:26. Washington is 2-3-0 in its last five, lost that game at NJD, and is missing Vincent Desharnais. The Devils sit second in the Metropolitan, eight points ahead of fourth-place Washington.

Our numbers favor New Jersey at 3.3 expected goals to 2.95. At five on five the Devils have 58% of the expected goals to Washington's 53%. Their power play (0.79 expected goals a game) faces a penalty kill that allows 0.84, and the Capitals take 4.2 penalties a game. In goal, projected starters Connor Hellebuyck (+1.9 goals saved above expected this season) and Logan Thompson (+1.4) are close this year, though Thompson was +28.2 last season to Hellebuyck's +3.4.

Jack Hughes, on a seven-game point streak, is our top pick to score at 41%. Alex Tuch leads Washington at 36%. Luke Evangelista, one goal from 50 career, is at 21%, and Jesper Bratt has ten points in six games against the Capitals. Among our under-the-radar picks, third-liner Arseny Gritsyuk has produced 2.6 expected goals in his last 10 games, and we have him at 22% to score. He's a player to watch, not a lock.
